subject: Banking
title: SPACs and Blank Check Companies
description: A micro-lesson that makes SPACs and Blank Check Companies usable.

hook.text: A SPAC raises money through an IPO with no business. It is a blank check company that promises to buy something later.

buildup.text: In 2021, SPACs raised $162 billion. Companies used them to go public faster.

discovery.text: SPAC sponsors earn 20% of shares for free, called the promote.

twist.text: By 2023, most SPAC mergers had destroyed value. The average SPAC stock dropped 50% or more after the deal closed.

climax.text: SPACs were a loophole around IPO rules that mostly benefited sponsors.

punchline.text: $162 billion raised, most lost. SPACs enriched sponsors, not investors.

quiz.question: What is the SPAC sponsor's 'promote'?
options: A free 20% stake in the company for organizing the deal
